title: The ache of missing God
hookLine: the gopis miss Krishna so much that the wise man sent to teach them learns bhakti from them
carry: missing God is a mark of bhakti
tomorrow: can you find something you never lost?

lines: A WISE MAN SENT TO COMFORT.
cards: Krishna has left the village of Vraja for the city of Mathura, and he hasn't come back. The cowherd women who loved him, the gopis, can't stop talking about him.
So he sends his friend Uddhava, a wise and learned man, with a message: I was never really apart from you; turn your minds inward and you'll find me. Uddhava arrives to comfort them.
In the Bhagavata Purana, he ends up being the one who's taught.

teach.h: THE GOPIS WEEP; A BEE GETS AN EARFUL.
teach.b: The gopis hear the message, and they weep. One of them talks to a passing bee as if it were Krishna's messenger, half angry, half in love. They don't want a lesson; they want him.
And Uddhava, the man of knowledge, is undone.

teach.h: UDDHAVA: LET ME BE A BUSH IN VRAJA.
teach.b: He stays for months, and before he goes he says he'd gladly be a bush or a creeper in Vraja, just to be touched by the dust of those women's feet.
Many teachers read it this way: knowledge came to teach love, and love taught knowledge. And a short Sanskrit book, the Narada Bhakti Sutras, points to the gopis as its example.
Having defined bhakti as supreme love, it asks: what are its marks? Three teachers answer first. Vyasa: fondness for worship, the lamp and the flowers.
Garga: fondness for the stories of the Lord. Shandilya: delight in the Self.
Then Narada's own view: bhakti is offering every action to the Lord, and feeling deep anguish on forgetting him. The word is vyakulata: turmoil, the way a parent feels who loses a child in a crowd.

teach.h: MISSING GOD IS A MARK OF BHAKTI.
teach.b: Here's the teaching, one of Hinduism's most tender: missing God isn't a failure of devotion. It's one of its marks. Bhakti poets call love in separation viraha, and they've sung it for centuries.
The sutras add one guardrail: even the gopis never forgot who Krishna was. So if your puja has slipped, many teachers would say the ache you feel isn't the door closing. It's the door.

how: In many Vaishnava homes and temples, songs of longing for Krishna, often in the gopis' voice, are sung at evening aarti and in kirtan; poets call this love in separation viraha. Devotion also takes the other shapes the sutras name: daily puja, retelling the stories, and offering one's work to God.

o: the duty to perform rituals without any feeling
devotion, with marks like worship, stories, joy and longing
a quiet study of texts, with no feeling involved

games.q: four teachers on bhakti — tap the pairs.
p: fondness for talk of the Lord

s: if you feel far from God, your devotion has failed
Narada counts anguish on forgetting the Lord as a mark of bhakti, not a failure of it.
the sutras give the gopis of Vraja as the example of bhakti
the cowherd women who loved Krishna, and missed him, are named as the instance.
the sutras say the gopis forgot Krishna's greatness
they head that off: even the gopis did not forget his greatness.

games.q: your aunt hasn't been to the temple in months. she says she feels far from God and guilty about it. by Narada's sutras, what's true?
o: that ache is itself a mark of bhakti, and it can turn her back.
devotion only counts if the rituals are kept every day.
feeling far away shows she was never really devoted.
games.why: sutra nineteen: offering every act, and deep anguish on forgetting him. the gopis missed Krishna, and the sutras call them the model.

practice: If you pray, say one name of God you love, Krishna, Rama, Shiva, Devi, slowly, a few times, the way many Hindus do in japa. Between the names, notice any small ache of distance. Don't fix it; Narada counts it as love.
If you don't pray, do the same with the name of someone you miss, and let the missing be what it is: a sign of how much they matter.

wordCard.voice: Bhakti. Devotion. Vyasa sees it in worship, Garga in the stories, Shandilya in delight, and Narada in the ache of forgetting. The gopis lived all four.

orig.note: Sanskrit vyākulatā, turmoil, distress: Narada's mark of bhakti is this anguish on forgetting the Lord.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: missing God is a mark of bhakti. The gopis knew it. Day six hundred ninety-four, done.

sources.ref: Narada Bhakti Sutras 15–19 (the views of Vyasa, Garga, Shandilya and Narada)
Narada Bhakti Sutras 21–24 (the gopis of Vraja; the secret lover)
Bhagavata Purana 10.46–47 (Uddhava sent to Vraja; the gopis' grief and the bee; Uddhava's wish to be a plant in Vrindavan)
